column4: The exact same back view of this porcelain maid on the same flat ivory paper, same pose, same hair, same dress, same scale and position. Change only the wind-up key: it protrudes straight out of the middle of her back toward the viewer, so from directly behind we see it edge-on. Draw a small round brass mount plate on the coal dress between the shoulder blades just above the white apron bow, with the key's bow seen edge-on as a single thin vertical coal bar (about the length of the original key's height) crossing the mount, the two loops collapsed into the bar. Do not show the round loops face-on.

The exact same three-quarter side view of this porcelain maid on the same flat ivory paper, same pose, hair, dress, scale and position. Fix only the wind-up key: remove the key floating beside her hair, and instead attach it to the middle of her back between the shoulder blades, just above the white apron bow at waist level. A short shaft sticks straight out backwards from her back, and at its end the key's bow (two round loops joined by a hub, coal with a thin orange rim) stands upright, seen nearly face-on from this side angle. The key clearly connects to her back.

The exact same cathedral interior, same camera, same pews, same number and placement of hooded congregants as the first reference (every figure in exactly the same spot and size). Change only their heads: every hooded figure has raised its head high and tilted it far back to stare up at the stage and the window above. The hoods slide back so each figure shows a clearly upturned coal profile of chin and throat, the hood's opening now faces up and forward instead of down. The difference from the first reference must be obvious at a glance in every row.
